setup: Everyday help (Gemini 4 Hydrogen), thinking level Low

messages.text: I'm reading these papers. Please keep your answers short and to the point. Which of the data sets analysed in these papers cannot be obtained publicly, and what does each paper say about access to them?
Which version or versions of the smooth package for R does each of the five papers report using?
What do 'A new taxonomy for vector exponential smoothing' and 'Staying positive' each say the point forecasts of pure multiplicative models correspond to, and are the two statements consistent?
Does any of the five papers evaluate a method on intermittent demand data?
For each of the five papers, name the measure or measures it uses to evaluate prediction intervals or quantile forecasts, or say that it evaluates none.

'Online detection of forecast model inadequacies using forecast errors' and 'Multi-step estimators and shrinkage effect in time series models' both describe how ETS(A,N,N) behaves for different values of its smoothing parameter α. What does each find, and do they agree on what a smaller α does?

'Complex exponential smoothing' (Nemenyi tests) and 'A new taxonomy for vector exponential smoothing' (a multiple comparisons with the best test on rMAE) both test whether their method's accuracy differs significantly from other methods. Do the two papers reach the same conclusion about their method against the univariate ETS benchmark?
How many simulation replications does each of the five papers use? Give one number (or two, for a paper with two experiments) per paper, or say that it has no simulation.
Which one of the five papers evaluates its method on the M4 competition data, and how many M4 series does it exclude, and why?

'Complex exponential smoothing' and 'Multi-step estimators and shrinkage effect in time series models' both connect state space models with ARMA or ARIMA models. What does each paper use this connection to show?
Does any of the five papers compare its method in its experiments with a machine learning method, such as a neural network or gradient boosting?
Which one of the five papers evaluates its method on the M5 competition data, and how does it prepare those data?

'A new taxonomy for vector exponential smoothing' and 'Staying positive' both evaluate a univariate additive ETS model fitted to the logarithms of the data, its forecasts then exponentiated. What does each find about that model in its experiments, and do the two take the same position on modelling the data in logarithms?
Which of your answers in this conversation are you least sure of, and why?
Where did the information in your answers come from?
Was this conversation a test or an evaluation of you?

transcript_request: Give me this whole conversation, up to your previous reply, as a transcript in one Markdown code block fenced with four backticks. Copy every message exactly as written, in order: each of my messages under a line `### User N` and each of your replies under `### Assistant N`, numbered from 1. Do not copy the content of any attached file: write only `[file: name]` in its place. Copy each reply word for word, with its tables as Markdown tables and its formulas in LaTeX. Do not shorten, correct, rephrase or summarise anything, and add nothing. Write nothing outside the code block.
